label: Netonix WS-12-250-DC WISP Switch
description: Managed passive-PoE WISP switch: 12x 1G RJ45, every port a configurable 24V/48V/24VH/48VH PoE source, plus 2x 1G SFP uplinks. 9-72 VDC input (positive DC only) so it can run straight off a battery bank; 250 W ceiling.

poe.note: 250 W ceiling. Netonix publishes no separate PoE budget, only the unit's maximum power consumption - and the store page for this model is explicit that the PoE budget is a function of input voltage: 250 W above 12 V in, 200 W above 11 V, 150 W below 10 V. The switch's own draw comes out of that figure, so treat 250 W as the ceiling and not as headroom.

fabric.note: Netonix publishes 'Total Non-Blocking Line Rate' as the sum of one-directional port bandwidth (12x1G + 2x1G = 14 Gbps; 24x1G + 2x1G = 26 Gbps), not the duplex-doubled figure other vendors print as 'switching capacity'. Like for like with a FortiSwitch's 128 Gbps for 24x1G + 4x10G, these are half the number: 28 Gbps and 52 Gbps duplex.

notes: Spec sheet (https://netonix.com/media/wysiwyg/ws-specsheet.pdf): 223 x 181 x 44 mm, 2 kg, 9-72 VDC positive-ground-only input, 250 W maximum consumption, forced-air cooling with fan RPM monitoring, Vitesse switch core, MIPS 24K 416 MHz, 128 MB RAM, 16 MB flash, -25 to 55 C, 5-95% non-condensing, CE/FCC/IC, 24 kV air and contact ESD. Ports: 12x 10/100/1000 plus 2 SFP; the faceplate labels the cages 13/14. 24VH is available on ports 1-2 and 48VH on ports 1-4 only - the high-current mode is a property of those ports, not of the whole box. 48 V output can be set to pass the input voltage through. The vendor warns these units are not for negative 48 V plant: using -48 V damages the switch (no isolated input/output); the WS-26-400-IDC is the isolated model. Passive PoE, software-configurable per port in the UI/CLI, not 802.3af/at: 24V and 48V at 1 A on pins 4,5(+)/7,8(-), 24VH and 48VH at 2 A on pins 1,2,4,5(+)/3,6,7,8(-) pairs. Current sensor per port. A port's wattage is therefore set by the voltage and current limit a human picks, which is why the port carries no wattage class here - only the unit's published ceiling does. Software from the same spec sheet: LACP/static LAG, STP/RSTP/MSTP/ERPS, port mirroring, VLAN dot1Q/QinQ/port trunking, SNMP, SMTP alerts, per-port bandwidth limiting, QoS, per-port ping watchdog, scheduled port bouncing, cable diagnostics, loop protection, DHCP snooping, IGMP snooping, flow control, storm control, multicast filtering, port isolation, auto TFTP backup on config change, UDP (Ubiquiti discovery), CDP and LLDP, ACLs plus login tarpit. Nothing in the sheet routes IP between VLANs, so this is l2-forward only. Management is HTTPS on 192.168.1.20 (admin/admin) with the host on 192.168.1.0/24, and a RS-232 serial console at 115200 8-N-1, no parity, XON/XOFF flow control, null-modem cable.
